items.followUp: Define a community and give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies the organisms and the shared place and time that define a population.
rubric.description: A group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition, including same species and a shared area or habitat; the definition must also indicate that the organisms live there together (at the same time).

rubric.why: Recognizes the ecological term being defined.
rubric.description: Correctly identifies the group as a population.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the group a population.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of individuals of the same species living in the same area at the same time.

items.followUp: What is a qualitative observation? Give one example.

rubric.why: Quantitative observations are expressed through numbers or measurements.
rubric.description: States that quantitative observations involve numbers, counts or measurements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the observation is numerical or measured.

rubric.why: A suitable example shows an observation expressed numerically or measured.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a quantitative observation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example; award only if the example is expressed as a count or measurement.

modelAnswer: Quantitative observations are based on measurements or counts and are expressed in numbers.
For example, the length of a leaf is 10 cm.

items.followUp: How does diffusion differ from active transport?

rubric.why: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient.
rubric.description: States the direction of movement against the concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for indicating movement from lower to higher concentration, or against the concentration gradient.

rubric.why: Movement against the gradient requires energy.
rubric.description: States that active transport requires energy, usually supplied by ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning energy or ATP.

modelAnswer: Active transport is the movement of substances across a cell membrane against their concentration gradient.
It requires energy, usually supplied by ATP.

items.followUp: Write the scientific names of a cat and a mango plant.

rubric.why: This is the scientific name of humans.
rubric.description: Writes the scientific name of human.

rubric.why: This is the scientific name of pea.
rubric.description: Writes the scientific name of pea.

items.followUp: State two characteristics of organisms in kingdom Fungi.

rubric.why: Protists have cells with a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
rubric.description: States that protists are eukaryotic organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying protists as eukaryotic.

rubric.why: Most protists are unicellular, a key characteristic commonly used to describe the kingdom.
rubric.description: States that most protists are unicellular.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are mostly single-celled.

modelAnswer: Kingdom Protista consists mainly of unicellular eukaryotic organisms.

items.followUp: What occurs during the G1 phase of interphase?

rubric.why: DNA is copied during the S phase.
rubric.description: States that DNA is replicated during the S phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning DNA replication or synthesis.

rubric.why: The S phase is one of the stages of interphase.
rubric.description: Identifies the S phase as a stage of interphase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating the S phase in interphase.

modelAnswer: The S phase (synthesis phase) is the part of interphase during which DNA is replicated.
As a result, each chromosome is duplicated.

items.followUp: What is synapsis, and during which stage of meiosis does it occur?

rubric.why: Crossing over involves the exchange of chromosome segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.description: Defines crossing over as exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the exchange of segments and identifying the chromatids or homologous chromosomes involved.

rubric.why: Crossing over produces new combinations of genetic material.
rubric.description: Gives genetic variation as an advantage of crossing over.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that crossing over increases genetic variation or creates new gene combinations.

modelAnswer: Crossing over is the exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis.
It produces genetic variation in the offspring.

items.followUp: How does cytokinesis occur in animal cells?

rubric.why: Plant cytokinesis occurs through formation of a cell plate that grows outward between the daughter cells.
rubric.description: States that a cell plate forms in the middle of the plant cell and grows outward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the cell plate or explaining its inward-to-outward formation.

rubric.why: Animal cells divide by a cleavage furrow that constricts inward from the cell surface.
rubric.description: Contrasts plant cytokinesis with the inward constriction of a cleavage furrow in animal cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the animal-cell cleavage furrow or clearly contrasting it with plant-cell cytokinesis.

modelAnswer: In plant cells, a cell plate forms in the middle of the cell and grows outward until it joins the cell wall.
In animal cells, a cleavage furrow forms at the cell surface and constricts inward.
